extra.message: In UsersHandler.post, the username and password parameters from self.get_argument('username')/'password' are concatenated directly into a SQL query string passed to cur.execute(), with no parameterization or escaping. An attacker can submit a username/password such as "' OR '1'='1" to bypass authentication or extract data via SQL injection.

In ServerHandler.post, the 'server' request parameter is taken directly from user input via self.get_argument('server') and concatenated into a shell command string passed to os.popen('ping -c 3 ' + server). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; cat /etc/passwd' or '$(whoami)') to execute arbitrary OS commands.

In ContentHandler.get, the 'file' request argument is concatenated directly into a filesystem path ('read/' + file_name) with no sanitization of path traversal sequences. A request such as /read?file=../../../../etc/passwd allows an attacker to read arbitrary files on the server accessible to the process.

StaticHandler.get builds the file path by naively concatenating the URL-captured 'path' group ('static/' + path) with no normalization or containment check before opening the file with io.open/open. A request like /static/../server.py or /static/..%2f..%2fserver.py can escape the 'static/' directory and read arbitrary files on disk (e.g. server.py, test.db, or other files readable by the process).

SearchHandler.get (server.py line 87-89) passes the unsanitized 'q' request parameter directly to search.html as 'query' and 'link'. The template renders both with the {% raw %} directive (lines 70 and 71), which explicitly disables Tornado's default HTML autoescaping. This allows a classic reflected XSS: a request like /search?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> is rendered verbatim into the page and executed in the victim's browser. The handler also explicitly sets 'X-XSS-Protection: 0' (server.py line 88), disabling the browser's built-in XSS filter as a compensating control.

SearchHandler.get explicitly disables the browser's XSS auditor by setting the response header 'X-XSS-Protection: 0'. Combined with the {% raw %} reflected XSS sink in search.html, this removes a defense-in-depth mitigation and makes exploitation more reliable in older browsers that support the header.

cwe: CWE-116: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output

extra.message: UsersHandler.post logs the raw request body via print("POST ", self.request.uri, "\nBODY ", self.request.body), which includes the plaintext username and password submitted by the user. This writes sensitive credentials to the server's stdout/log stream, where they may be persisted, rotated into log aggregation systems, or exposed to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: create_db() creates the Users table and seeds it with plaintext passwords (e.g. 'admin'/'admin'), and UsersHandler.post later compares the submitted password directly against this plaintext column with no hashing. Passwords are never hashed at rest, so a database compromise (or the SQL injection in this same handler) directly exposes every user's real password.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: create_db() hardcodes a set of default user credentials directly in source code, including an 'admin'/'admin' account. If this database-seeding path is ever run against a real deployment (or the shipped test.db is deployed as-is), these well-known credentials grant an attacker a working, potentially privileged login.

The Tornado Application is configured with "debug": True. In production this enables the auto-reloader and, more importantly, Tornado's debug error pages, which render full stack traces (including source code and local variables) to the client on unhandled exceptions, leaking internal implementation details useful to an attacker.

UploadHandler.post accepts any uploaded file with no validation of content-type, extension, or file size/content, writing it to /tmp with an attacker-influenced extension (derived from the original filename) and predictable-ish random 6-character name. There is no allowlist of permitted file types, enabling storage of arbitrary/executable content on disk and potential disk-exhaustion (no size limit enforced).

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
